_finding: The owner asked the dashboard to say who is not counted, after his own visits had been counted for days. The block must be on the page, and it must warn when nothing is set yet or when the server cannot read its own addresses: a block that looks fine in that state is worse than no block, because it says the opposite of the truth.

mutations.name: the block is not on the page
mutations.find: ${card('MCP calls', topList(ts?.mcp_calls, { limit: 7, cls: 'mcp' }), { sub: when })}${notCounted(ignoring)}
mutations.replace: ${card('MCP calls', topList(ts?.mcp_calls, { limit: 7, cls: 'mcp' }), { sub: when })}
mutations.expect: FAIL ...it says who is not counted, in counts and a date, and never an address

mutations.name: nothing set and unreadable addresses look like any other row
mutations.find:
const row = (k, v, cls = '') => `
  • ${esc(k)}${esc(v)}
    • `
mutations.expect: FAIL ...and says so when nothing is set or the server cannot read its own addresses

mutations.name: the empty card says none again, without why
mutations.expect: FAIL ...an empty "Who called a tool" says only checkers called

mutations.name: the checkers that called are not counted
mutations.find: const checkerUsers = ts ? Math.max(0, num(ts.mcp_use_agents) - num(ts.mcp_agent_use_agents)) : 0
mutations.expect: FAIL ...an empty "Who called a tool" says only checkers called

mutations.name: a day written before the view reads as only checkers
mutations.expect: FAIL ...an empty "Who called a tool" says only checkers called
